title: Arcana Famiglia

routes.title: リベルタルート
routes.notes: Libertà (リベルタ). Available from the very first playthrough, no unlock conditions. Recommended as the 5th route (last of the 5 always-open routes) by manga-daisuki.net's suggested order.

routes.title: パーチェルート
routes.notes: Parche (パーチェ), Clubs department executive. Available from the very first playthrough, no unlock conditions. Consistently recommended as the first or an early route by both a full walkthrough (choro-game.com) and a review/impressions blog (manga-daisuki.net). Has multiple endings (ED1/ED2/ED3 pattern per choro-game), including a defeat/bad ending tied to losing the final デュエロ (duel).

routes.title: デビトルート
routes.notes: Debito (デビト), Coins department executive. Available from the very first playthrough, no unlock conditions. Recommended as the 2nd route by manga-daisuki.net's suggested order.

routes.title: ルカルート
routes.notes: Luca (ルカ). Available from the very first playthrough, no unlock conditions. Recommended as the 3rd route by manga-daisuki.net's suggested order.

routes.title: ノヴァルート
routes.notes: Nova (ノヴァ), Holy Chalice department executive. Available from the very first playthrough, no unlock conditions. Recommended as the 4th route by manga-daisuki.net's suggested order.

routes.title: ジョーリィルート
routes.notes: Jolly / Jolie (ジョーリィ). LOCKED: the ruRi hatenablog full walkthrough explicitly states this route is 「２周目以降ルート解放」(unlocks from the 2nd playthrough onward), so the actual mechanical requirement is at least one prior completed playthrough, not clearance of all five initially available routes. In this guide's recommended order, Parche is cleared first, so `prerequisites: ["parche"]` is sufficient to represent that unlock without overstating the requirement. A separate review blog (momokan.chu.jp, via search snippet) recommends Jolly last and describes him as the 'final boss' of the character select screen; that is recommendation/context, not an additional mechanical lock. Jolly remains 6th here because Dante's special endings require all other characters, including Jolly, to be cleared.

routes.title: ダンテルート
routes.notes: Dante (ダンテ), chief of the Intelligence division. LOCKED: both full walkthroughs (choro-game.com and ruRi hatenablog) explicitly state 「２周目以降ルート解放」(unlocks from the 2nd playthrough onward). Additionally, both sources state that this route's three main endings — 【ファミリアED】(Famiglia End, also called 第１０のカード『ルオータ・デラ・フォルトゥナ』/ 'Wheel of Fortune' the 10th card), 【ノーマルED】(Normal End), and 【敗北ED】(Defeat End) — are gated: 「全員を攻略後ED回収が可能になります」(these can only be obtained after clearing everyone/all other characters). The Famiglia End is treated as the game's true/best ending and is only reachable once all 6 other character routes (Liberta, Nova, Debito, Parche, Luca, Jolly) have been cleared, making Dante the mandatory final route despite one lower-confidence review blog (manga-daisuki.net) suggesting Dante before Jolly. Marked is_true_ending because the Famiglia ED / Wheel of Fortune ending is gated behind clearing every other route, matching the 'true end' pattern (see disagreements).

sources.title: アルカナ・ファミリア -La storia della Arcana Famiglia- Ancora 攻略 (choro / 乙女ゲーム攻略ブログ)
sources.notes: Complete guide hub for the PS Vita 'Ancora' port (same VNDB entry v8203 as Rinato), linking to full individual choice-by-choice walkthroughs for all 7 routes: Liberta (blog-entry-1309.html), Nova (blog-entry-1367.html), Debito (blog-entry-1311.html), Parche (blog-entry-1368.html), Luca (blog-entry-1284.html), Dante (blog-entry-1364.html), Jolly (blog-entry-1334.html). Each page contains dated (4/1–6/1) choice text, SAVE1/SAVE2/SAVE3 markers, デュエロ (duel) success/fail outcomes (△/□/×), and ED1/ED2/ED3 ending labels. Confirms Dante's route restriction ('２周目以降ルート解放') and that his 3 special endings (ファミリアED/ノーマルED/敗北ED) require all other 6 characters cleared first ('全員を攻略後ED回収が可能'). Primary source for full choice-tree content and Dante/Jolly lock confirmation.

sources.title: アルカナ・ファミリア Rinato 個別攻略 (ruRiの気ままにオタ活)
sources.notes: Complete exact-target Nintendo Switch Rinato walkthrough covering all 7 character routes. Uses Switch button notation (for example YXY where Vita/Ancora uses △□△), dated choice text, MAP/Select/Cocoaru steps, duel success/failure paths, and ending cleanup. Adopted as Set B for target-facing reconciliation; jpGuide2 excerpts are kept verbatim to this Rinato page rather than Vita symbols.

sources.title: [PSvita] アルカナ・ファミリア無印はキャラが魅力的すぎた！オススメの攻略順とキャラ別感想 (乙女ゲーム大好記)
sources.notes: Review/impressions blog (not a choice-by-choice walkthrough) but explicitly states a numbered recommended route order under the heading 'キャラクターのおすすめ攻略順': 1.パーチェ 2.デビト 3.ルカ 4.ノヴァ 5.リベルタ 6.ダンテ 7.ジョーリィ. Notes the author personally played in a different order and adds 'シナリオとしては壮大なネタバレなどもないので、好きな順番でプレイしたら良いと思う' (no major spoilers between routes, so preferred order is fine) for the 5 unlocked routes. Used as supplementary corroboration for the first 5 routes' order; its Dante-before-Jolly placement is treated as lower-confidence than the two full walkthroughs' explicit unlock-condition text (see disagreements).

sources.title: Nintendo Switch/Steam『アルカナ・ファミリア Rinato』公式サイト - STORY

Confirms the main story premise (Arcana Duello tournament, April 1 to June 1 timeframe) and character roles (Mondo as boss/father, Sumire as his wife, Nova/Parche/Debito/Dante as department executives). sources.title: 「アルカナ・ファミリア Rinato」Switch版は7月24日に発売！ (Gamer)
sources.notes: Exact Rinato release announcement based on publisher information. Explicitly identifies Rinato as a port of the 2015 PS Vita Ancora release and enumerates the port changes as system/battle-presentation polish, higher-resolution graphics, new package art, and multilingual subtitles. It does not announce new or rewritten scenario/route content. This is strong target-applicability evidence for Ancora walkthrough structure, but it is not itself a Rinato choice-by-choice walkthrough.

disagreements: 1) Dante vs. Jolly final order: manga-daisuki.net (a review/impressions blog, not a full choice-tree walkthrough) lists its personal recommended order as ...リベルタ→ダンテ→ジョーリィ (Dante 6th, Jolly last/7th). However, both of the two full choice-by-choice walkthroughs used as primary sources (choro-game.com and ruRi hatenablog) independently state that Dante's three notable endings (ファミリアED / ノーマルED / 敗北ED, including the Famiglia End '第10のカード ルオータ・デラ・フォルトゥナ') can only be obtained '全員を攻略後' (after clearing everyone/all other characters) — which necessarily includes Jolly, since Jolly is one of the 7 routes. This guide follows the two full-walkthrough primary sources and places Jolly before Dante, with Dante last, since otherwise Dante's true/Famiglia ending would be unreachable at the point the guide reaches it. 2) Whether Dante's Famiglia ED constitutes a distinct 'true end' separate from a normal character route: no source uses the exact phrase 真エンド (true end), but the gating of the Famiglia ED behind clearing all other 6 routes, plus its explicit '第10のカード' (10th/final tarot card) framing distinguishing it from the other 6 characters' single-route endings, matches the standard 'true end' pattern used elsewhere in this repository's guides; it is flagged is_true_ending on the dante route on that basis. 3) The first 5 routes (Parche, Debito, Luca, Nova, Liberta) have no documented mechanical locks or prerequisites in either full walkthrough — the order used here follows manga-daisuki.net's suggested order for lack of any conflicting source, and could be freely reordered among themselves without affecting route access. 4) momokan.chu.jp and the PSP-era wiki at arcana.stgtk.com could not be directly fetched (DNS resolution failures for both domains during this session) despite appearing in search results; their content is treated as unverified/supplementary and was not used as a primary source. No English guide was located or used; per the brief, Japanese sources take full precedence and none was needed as even a supplementary reference given two solid full Japanese walkthroughs were found. 5) Revalidation note (2026-09-25): Set A remains the directly inspected Ancora/Vita walkthrough at choro-game.com, while Set B is now a directly inspected exact-target Rinato/Nintendo Switch walkthrough at ruRi. Rinato release documentation identifies the Switch title as a port of Ancora and the exact-target Set B provides target-platform choice/duel text. Exact-target disagreements, including the Jolly ordinary-choice difference documented above, are preserved rather than silently normalized.
